 Crime Hyderabad Hyderabad Police Raid SmokinSpot Over Banned Vape Sales Through WhatsApp and Rapido
 saniya anwar 12 Nov 2026 7:02 PM Share this: HYDERABAD: The Telangana EAGLE Force and Raidurgam police have busted an alleged network selling banned e-cigarettes through WhatsApp orders and app-based deliveries, arresting an outlet manager and seizing 46 vapes and other material.
 The police seized 49 packets of foreign cigarettes, two mobile phones and two payment scanners from the outlet, identified as SmokinSpot. The vapes were allegedly sold for between ₹2,800 and ₹4,000 each. 
 Investigators estimate that around 107 devices were sold during October and November 2026. Customers allegedly placed orders through WhatsApp, made payments either digitally or in cash, and received the products through Rapido delivery services.
 Gold rate today in Hyderabad, November 13: 22K at ₹1,26,950, 24K at ₹1,38,490
 Police probe interstate supply links and financial transactions 
 The investigation has reportedly identified suppliers based in Kerala and Karnataka. Police are examining the suspected interstate supply chain, payment records and delivery network to establish the roles of suppliers and other persons involved.
 Investigators suspect the racket could be linked to a wider illegal trade estimated at more than ₹10 crore. The figure and the alleged links are being examined as part of the probe. 
 The latest seizure comes amid a series of operations by the EAGLE Force against the sale of prohibited e-cigarettes in Hyderabad. In a raid at Sainikpuri on October 27, the force seized 39 e-cigarettes, a payment scanner and three mobile phones. Police said the two suspects allegedly used WhatsApp to communicate with customers and digital payments to collect money. Investigators had identified around 45 customers in Hyderabad and 26 deliveries since August 3 in that case.
 In another operation in September, EAGLE Force sleuths and Madhapur police arrested three employees during raids on two outlets. Police said bank records showed that ₹2.3 crore had been credited to two accounts linked to the accused over about two years, while investigators identified 351 buyers, including 130 from Hyderabad.
 E-cigarette sales and online distribution prohibited 
 The Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019, prohibits the production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, storage and advertisement of electronic cigarettes. The Union health ministry reiterated the prohibition on online sales in an advisory issued on January 22, 2025, asking states to take action against sellers using e-commerce sites, mobile applications and other internet-based platforms.
 The EAGLE Force said its statewide crackdown had resulted in 11 cases, 18 arrests and the seizure of 1,619 boxes of vapes, with 21 people still absconding.
 Further investigation is under way into the suspected international supply routes, financial transactions and delivery networks.
